review_surface_coverage.description: Coverage of the review surfaces (traust-contracts enums/v1/review-surface.json): one entry per surface, recording whether the audit answered it with a finding, a negative result, not-applicable, or not assessed. A deterministic record, so coverage is checked by schema, not inferred from prose. llm-integration is allowed but not in required: the report checks require it for audits dated from 2026-11-02, so earlier reports stay valid.

disposition_summary.$comment: Present only on cumulative reports (*-findings-current.json) generated by the track-findings skill from a disposition layer (layer.schema.json). Absent on audit-stage reports.

ref.$comment: Optional (harness >= 0.122.0, branch-awareness Phase 0): the branch or tag name as checked out for this audit (e.g. 'release-4.19', 'main', 'v1.2.3'). Explicit ref provenance — when present, preferred over report-slug parsing; the legacy slug-suffix parsing remains the fallback for older corpus data. Never required; all existing reports stay valid.

ref_kind.$comment: Optional (harness >= 0.122.0): what metadata.ref names — 'branch' = an explicitly requested non-default branch (counts as a branch re-audit in the census), 'tag' = a tag checkout, 'default' = the repository default branch (metadata.ref still records its name, e.g. 'main'), 'stream' (harness >= 0.140.0) = a dist-git release stream (c10s, c9s) — a mainline deliverable audited in its own right, NEVER a branch re-audit. Writers set ref and ref_kind together.

loc_reviewed.description: Total lines of source code reviewed. Prefer an integer; string is accepted for backward compatibility with earlier reports.

loc_breakdown.description: Structured lines-of-code count for the audited ref, produced by tokei/cloc/scc.

tool.description: Tool used to compute the count (tokei, cloc, scc, wc).

excludes.description: Paths or globs excluded from the count (e.g. vendor/, node_modules/).

additional.description: Producer-declared provenance and run records. harness_version identifies the producing harness release; contracts_version pins the contract surface it was validated against. The other declared fields are the run records the report-producing skills (code, rpm and container profiles) specify. The object stays open: an undeclared key is allowed, but a declared key must match its shape.

harness_version.description: Semver (+ optional -sha) of the producing harness release. Its presence marks the report as modern-producer output, which requires stamped finding identity (see the root allOf rule).

contracts_version.description: Version of traust-contracts this report was validated against.

deterministic_steps.description: Fate of every deterministic pre-scan, keyed by step name (e.g. opengrep, gitleaks, osv-scanner, sbom-grype, k8s-hardening, priv-profile, fork-advisory-lag, route-guards, config-matrix, yara, crypto-audit, crypto). Value: 'ran', 'skipped: <reason>', or a step-specific state ('list', '<n> records'). A skipped step means that area was reviewed by hand only; consumers must not read missing scanner facts as a clean result.

precision_gates.description: Precision Gate pass record. A report that files critical/high findings without this block is an incomplete run.

crit_high_evaluated.description: Every critical/high candidate evaluated, filed or gated.

fired.description: Each gate that changed a candidate's disposition. An empty list is legitimate.

gate.description: Gate name from the skill's Precision Gate section.

coverage_gaps.description: Systems a pre-scan or review lane could not examine (unexpanded config systems, unenumerated frameworks, classes a scoped audit did not cover). Aggregated fleet-wide: an audit that skipped something says so here instead of reading as clean.

tool.description: Pre-scan or lane that recorded the gap.

count.description: Number of files or items affected, when known.

assertive_inference.description: Assertive reporting posture for languages with thin or no deterministic rule coverage. Changes the report-or-omit decision only, never severity or validation_status.

trigger.description: Why the posture applied, e.g. 'thin per opengrep coverage block'.

companion_lanes.description: Other scan lanes the tree needs that this audit does not cover (e.g. 'cloud-config-audit' when IaC is present). A declaration only; the router turns it into worklist rows.

audit_passes.description: Number of independent review passes merged into the report. Recorded when it differs from the two-pass default.

model_routing.description: The routed model decision that produced the report.

registry_sha.description: Short sha of the model registry revision that made the decision.

source_audit.description: Container profile: path of the source repository's code-profile report that this image audit cross-links.

degraded.description: True when the run lost coverage (a lane or tool unavailable). A degraded report must not be read as full coverage.

audit_profile.description: Report profile discriminator: 'code' = secure-code-audit (source/manifest audit), 'rpm' = secure-rpm-audit (dist-git packaging audit), 'container' = secure-container-audit (registry image audit via skopeo/syft/grype). Shared finding/severity/ID vocabulary; framework sections differ by profile.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the artifact this finding concerns, including an artifact that SHOULD exist and does not (an absent SECURITY.md is still `SECURITY.md`). Never a repo-root marker: `.`, `/`, `./` and `/./` all canonicalize to empty, which collapses the ledger fingerprint to (repo, '', cwe). When a finding genuinely concerns no artifact (e.g. 'repository appears unmaintained'), use a controlled pseudo-path from enums/v1/repo-scope-path.json. Not a notes field: prose in this field silently feeds identity.
path.$comment: Enforcement is staged, following the P0.4 -> P6 precedent (backfill, then flip): the rule is declared here and checked by the harness gate at warning level while existing corpus findings are migrated; the pattern below and the identity module strict mode become errors once that lands. Do NOT add the pattern before the migration — it would invalidate every existing report. Proposed: "pattern": "^(?!\\.?/?$)(repo:[a-z-]+|[^\\n]{1,200})$".

id.$comment: Canonical (harness >= 0.12.0): {REPO_SLUG}-{SHORTSHA}-{NNN} — REPO_SLUG = repo name uppercased, [^A-Z0-9] -> '_', truncated to 24 chars; SHORTSHA = first 7 lowercase hex chars of the audited commit; NNN = 001-based sequence. The second alternative preserves validation of pre-0.12.0 reports; the validator hard-errors on it when harness_version >= 0.12.0.

owasp_llm_references.description: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) category IDs this finding falls under. Set on findings about LLM, agent or MCP application code; the category ID is cited, never OWASP text.

peach_references.description: PEACH tenant-isolation hardening parameter(s) this finding violates. Only set when the audited component is multi-tenant.

attack_pattern.$comment: Concrete attack scenario. Expected on every critical/high finding (validator strict mode warns when absent).

category.$comment: Recommended vocabulary (kebab-case; validator strict mode warns off-vocabulary for harness >= 0.15.0): injection, authentication, authorization, secrets-management, supply-chain, insecure-workload-config, network-exposure, cryptography, input-validation, path-traversal, cross-site-scripting, ssrf, resource-management, logging-monitoring, data-exposure, tenant-isolation.

kind.description: The finding kind, independent of validity. Historical findings may omit it.

validation_status.$comment: Historical validity spellings remain accepted by this base reader schema. Newly authored unjudged findings omit this optional field; null is not a validity value. New report admission uses the installed registry's canonical validity members and does not infer a judgment from static review, kind, actor, or source. Historical not_verified denotes no answer; corrected is a revision marker, not a validity answer; hardening is represented independently by finding kind. Core finding decisions and authenticated restatement operations own subsequent state changes. Existing source artifacts, stored bytes, and exact-run replay remain compatible.

origin.$comment: Historical/provider provenance retained for old sanctioned-append findings. Current Core source attribution comes from the assessment that first reports a finding, not a candidate origin override or a new baseline append. Unjudged new findings do not acquire a validity answer from their origin; omit optional validation_status where the source shape supports it. Source schemas that do not declare validation_status must not add it. Historical origin fields and source artifacts remain readable.

pqc_classification.$comment: Optional (harness >= 0.84.0): PQC relevance of this finding, assigned by table lookup against the PQC reference tables (ir8547-mapping, pqc-readiness-decision-tree) — never free-authored. Only set on PQC-relevant findings; absent elsewhere.

remediation_effort.$comment: Legacy effort labels remain valid for historical artifacts. Sizes xs–xl are added; canonical_write rejects legacy labels without inventing a size mapping. Blocking is independent.

blocked_external.description: An external dependency blocks this item; independent of effort size.

isolation_dimensions.$comment: Optional (harness >= 0.120.0): isolation-hardening dimension(s) this finding stresses, vocabulary shared with schema/isolation-review.schema.json. Only set when the finding stresses a tenant boundary in a multi-tenant service; absent elsewhere. PEACH is cited by name/URL only — never adapted text.

isolation_boundary.$comment: Optional (harness >= 0.120.0): free-form identifier of the tenant-facing interface this finding sits on — an interface name from peach_isolation_review.interfaces[] or an IF-n id from a service isolation review. Only meaningful alongside isolation_dimensions.

disposition.$comment: Present only on cumulative reports generated by the track-findings skill. disposition.validity must equal validation_status (validator-enforced).

fingerprint.description: Deterministic cross-scan identity: sha256(canonical repo URL | ';'-joined sorted set of lineless location paths | primary CWE). One implementation, the identity module fingerprint function; stamped by the finding-identity utility, never model-authored. Only the harness computes identity — a non-harness producer submits unstamped rather than inventing a value. Validation recomputes every stamp and compares (check_finding_identity), so a forged or drifted value is an error rather than a silent identity split. Secondary correlation key — the scan-scoped id stays the primary key, and a fingerprint is never the sole key of a disposition record.

fingerprint_algo.description: Algorithm version of `fingerprint` (the identity module ALGO_VERSION). Mirrors layer.schema.json's event field of the same name, and for the same reason: stamps outlive recipes, so matching fingerprints across an epoch boundary means comparing this field too. Absent on findings stamped before 2026-09-18 -- those predate the field rather than declaring an unknown version, and were separable only because exactly two recipes existed to try.

effective_severity.$comment: Present only on cumulative reports (harness >= 0.128.0): equals disposition.severity_override.severity when a human override exists, else the original severity. Original severity is never rewritten - severity-count cross-checks keep validating against the original field.

passes.description: Audit passes that independently surfaced this finding (dual-pass union-merge, harness >= 0.144.0). [1,2] = both passes; [2] = second pass only. Optional; single-pass reports omit it.

dependency.description: Supply-chain provenance for a dependency finding, so the finding is SELF-DESCRIBING and does not depend on a sibling impact-analysis artifact resolving by relative path. Required once findings live in object storage, and the join key for consumers that build their own database rather than reading the local SQLite projection. Optional; present when origin is 'impact-analysis' or the finding is otherwise advisory-derived.

advisory.description: Advisory id as published — CVE-, GHSA-, RHSA-, MAL-, PYSEC-, GO-, RUSTSEC-, OSV-.

module.description: Package identity in its ecosystem's native form (org.postgresql:postgresql, golang.org/x/crypto, lodash).

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem; the same vocabulary as impact-analysis metadata.ecosystem (enums/v1/ecosystem.json), including the distro ecosystems rpm/deb/apk for C/C++.

purl.description: Package URL when available — the portable identity for cross-system joins.

installed_version.description: Version observed in the manifest or SBOM that matched the range.

evidence_level.description: Tier that justified the classification; 'manifest' and 'symbol-usage' both ceiling at likely_affected.

impact_artifact.description: Reference to the impact-analysis artifact this was routed from. A provenance pointer, NOT the source of truth — the fields above stand alone if it cannot be resolved.

conflict.description: True when the layer contains both 'confirmed' and 'false_positive' validity events for this finding — surfaced for human re-review, never silently resolved.

refuted_awaiting_signoff.description: True when machine validation refuted the finding but no identity-provider-verified human has countersigned the false_positive determination yet.

assurance.description: Highest evidence class that has spoken on this finding's validity: execution_proven (reproducing exploit/crash), human_reviewed (identity-provider-verified human), machine_verified (triage/audit machine verdict), claimed (audit only).

fp_overridden.description: True when execution-verified evidence confirmed the finding over a prior human false_positive assertion. Surfaced loudly; the ledger preserves both events with attribution.

fp_reassertion_blocked.description: True when a single human false_positive assertion post-dates execution-verified confirmation — re-asserting FP against a reproducing PoC requires two independent identity-provider-verified humans (two-person rule).

events.description: event_id values from the disposition layer, chronological.

by.description: identity handle of the verified signer

at.description: when the override was made (occurred_at of the latest human severity event)

severity_override.description: Present only on cumulative reports when an identity-provider-verified human recorded a severity override in the disposition layer (latest human severity event wins). The finding's original severity field is preserved; effective_severity carries the override.

layer_ref.description: Relative path to the *-findings-layer.json this report was generated from.

conflicts.description: Finding IDs whose disposition.conflict is true.

needs_review_count.description: Count of pending items in the layer's needs_review queue.

severity_overrides.description: Every finding whose severity an identity-provider-verified human overrode via the countersign workbench (harness >= 0.128.0). Original severities stay in place; effective_severity carries the override per finding.

review_surface_entry.description: One review surface's outcome. finding: finding_ids name the report findings on it. negative: a negative_results entry whose area is the surface id records what was examined. not_applicable / not_assessed / out_of_scope: note says why; a not_assessed surface also belongs in metadata.additional.coverage_gaps. out_of_scope is for a diff-scoped scan whose diff does not touch the surface.

scan_review_surface_coverage.description: Review-surface coverage recorded by a scan that follows an audit (vuln-findings.schema.json, verification.schema.json). Same keys and statuses as the report's review_surface_coverage, but a scan has no negative_results, so a negative entry carries its evidence in note. The cumulative builder merges these records into the cumulative report.

scan_review_surface_entry.description: A review_surface_entry whose negative status also needs a note saying what was examined.

peach_isolation_review.description: PEACH tenant-isolation review. Records multi-tenancy applicability and, when applicable, one entry per customer-facing interface with its complexity, sharing model, boundary type, and P.E.A.C.H. hardening gaps.
peach_isolation_review.$comment: Required top-level section for harness >= 0.15.0 (validator-enforced, mirroring the canonical-ID gate): emit {applicable: false, rationale: <why>} for single-tenant components.

applicable.description: True if one deployment of this component serves more than one tenant/customer/trust domain.

rationale.description: Why the component is or is not multi-tenant.

shared.description: True if all tenants hit the same running instance; false if duplicated per tenant.

result.description: Free text; for per-fact judge decisions on deterministic pre-scan facts use the tokens 'promoted' or 'dismissed' so the precision tracker can compute per-rule precision.

rule_id.description: Scanner rule that produced the judged fact (e.g. an opengrep rule id).

finding_ids.description: Finding(s) the fact was promoted into; absent for dismissals.

effort.description: Ordered effort-size labels; null means unknown size. Blocking is independent, and no duration thresholds are defined.

roadmap_priority.description: Priority labels in numeric order; no urgency or deadline mapping is defined. P0-P4 are accepted uppercase spellings of p0-p4 (enums/v1/roadmap-priority.json): readers normalise them and writers store lowercase.

canonical_write.description: Opt-in canonical effort sizes or null for unknown size. Default historical validation is unchanged.

allOf.$comment: Identity is minted by the producing harness, never by a consumer. Any report that declares metadata.additional.harness_version MUST carry a fingerprint on every finding, so downstream consumers read stamped identity instead of recomputing it (divergent recomputation orphans ledger history). Legacy artifacts predating version stamping are exempt by having no harness_version.
